result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, though they are narrow and obstructed by utility poles. Parked vehicles provide a buffer from traffic but also create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the narrow sidewalk path, reducing the effective width for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both the left and right sidewalks

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles, specifically the white van on the right, block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street in the foreground

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street lined with row houses and a continuous concrete sidewalk. While the walkway is in good condition, there is no physical buffer from the roadway, and parked vehicles create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicle
hazards.description: A large van parked at the curb blocks the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane with no buffer, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and the roadway.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to ensure low vehicle speeds on this narrow residential street.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, but lacks any formal pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or traffic calming. The wide, unmarked roadway and presence of parallel parked cars create potential visibility issues for pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who may attempt to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the mid-ground

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks or pedestrian signage on a long, straight residential stretch may lead to higher vehicle speeds and unsafe crossing conditions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential context.
